findings.problem: TODO.md is the single largest same-file collision in the package and it is absent from the collision matrix entirely. Every one of the 175 briefs ends with the instruction 'If the task is a TODO.md close-out, check the box `- [ ]` -> `- [x]` on the source line and append ` — closed 2026-08-21 (TASK-nnn)`', i.e. 175 concurrent direct edits to one file, 107 of them inside global wave 1. Worse, 46 tasks share 20 TODO.md source LINES, and several of those pairs/triples are scheduled in the SAME wave (L10660 -> TASK-173/174/175 all wave 1; L4960 -> TASK-170/171 both wave 1; L4575 -> TASK-135/136 both wave 1; L2595 -> TASK-080/082/083/084 all wave 1; L8646 -> TASK-106/107 both wave 1; L0 -> TASK-158/159 both wave 1; L53 -> TASK-143/145 both wave 1) — those conflict on the same line, and semantically the box must not be checked until every sibling task lands. The master plan this package derives from warned about exactly this and prescribed the opposite shape.
findings.evidence: grep -rl 'check the box' --include='TASK-*.md' . | wc -l -> 175 (of 175 briefs). python: [t['id'] for t in tasks if 'TODO.md' in t['exact_files']] -> ['TASK-059'] only; 'TODO.md' in skeleton['collisions'] -> False. Duplicate-todo_line groups computed from skeleton: 20 lines shared by 46 tasks. Master plan docs/plans/2026-08-21-todo-completion-master-plan.md:210-212: '⚠️ **Every task in this wave collides on `TODO.md`.** Either run it serially, or have one agent verify all 37 and a single commit apply all the check-offs. The second shape is strongly preferred.'

fix.remove_from_briefs: Delete the 'check the box' clause from all 175 briefs.
fix.new_task: Add a single coordinator-owned close-out task (one commit, run after each wave merges) that checks off every TODO.md line whose covering tasks have all landed, keyed by todo_line -> set(task_ids).
fix.note: If the per-brief edit is kept instead, TODO.md must be added to skeleton['collisions'] with all 175 ids, which collapses the entire plan to a strictly serial 175-wave schedule.

findings.problem: internal/plugins/maintenance/plugin.go is the single registration point for every maintenance op (one `defs := []sdk.OperationDef{...}` literal). Ten tasks create a brand-new op file under internal/plugins/maintenance/ but do NOT list plugin.go in exact_files, so (a) the ops they build will never register — the op is written and unreachable, the exact failure shape recorded in project memory as 'Declaring you participate != being in the list' — and (b) the collision matrix shows plugin.go as a 3-task file (TASK-045/071/074) when it is really a 13-task hub, so those ten tasks are mis-waved and will conflict.

Otherwise add an acceptance criterion 'the op appears in `curl /api/v2/operations`' to each — a compile-clean unregistered op passes every current acceptance check.

findings.problem: The gate string shipped to 10 tasks is not a runnable shell command: `npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web test (web)` — the unquoted `(web)` is a subshell token and every POSIX shell/zsh fails to parse it. TASK-070's gate contains a literal `|` used as prose punctuation ('make ci  (Go) | npm --prefix web run lint ...'), which pipes go's output into npm. The per-workstream README/orchestration then concatenates the distinct gate strings with `;` into one command block presented as 'Gate for every task in this workstream', producing an unrunnable five-clause string that also re-runs the web suite three times.

gate.web-tasks: npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web test
gate.TASK-070: make ci && npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web test

fix.note: The '(Go)'/'(web)' annotations belong in prose, never inside the gate value. The workstream README should print the DISTINCT gate set as a list, not a `;`-joined command.

findings.problem: Waves are declared GLOBAL in BREAKDOWN but rendered as LOCAL in every workstream doc, and the two readings produce completely different schedules. BREAKDOWN §'Same-file collision rule' is subtitled 'drives wave ordering — GLOBAL across workstreams' and gives global counts (wave 1: 107 ... wave 8: 1). But web/README.md's wave table says 'Wave 2 | prereq: wave 1 merged + siblings rebased', and web/orchestration.md renders only web's own tasks in each subgraph. A coordinator working from web/orchestration.md starts TASK-161 once web's 11 wave-1 tasks merge; a coordinator working from BREAKDOWN waits for all 107. Under the local reading, cross-workstream collisions break outright: internal/config/config.go is serialized as wave1=TASK-016(config) ... wave7=TASK-070(maintenance), but maintenance's local wave 7 has no relationship to config's local wave 6, so TASK-021 and TASK-070 can run concurrently on config.go.

findings.problem: The wave barrier is a hard global gate ('A wave MUST NOT start while any of: the previous wave has an unmerged PR ...') over a wave-1 population of 107 tasks, against a stated concurrency cap of 4 workers. That is ~27 strictly serial 4-wide rounds — every one of them including the slowest task in the batch — before wave 2's 36 tasks may begin, and 5 of the 8 waves contain 4 tasks or fewer. The barrier buys nothing the pairwise collision edges do not already buy: two tasks with disjoint exact_files are safe regardless of which wave they are in.
findings.evidence: BREAKDOWN 'Waves: wave 1: 107, wave 2: 36, wave 3: 12, wave 4: 8, wave 5: 3, wave 6: 4, wave 7: 4, wave 8: 1.'; BREAKDOWN 'Concurrency cap: 4 workers at a time on this machine. 16 concurrent agents crashed the session on 2026-08-21.'; orchestration.md 'A wave MUST NOT start while any of: the previous wave has an unmerged PR; any sibling worktree is un-rebased; ...'.

fix.note: Replace the wave barrier with a ready-queue: a task is dispatchable when every task sharing one of its exact_files (and every depends_on) has merged. Same safety, no global stalls, and it degrades gracefully when one task blocks.

findings.evidence: skeleton TASK-069.gate = 'go build ./... && go test ./internal/maintenance/... (make ci is known-red on main per the plan doc; do not read a red make ci as a signal from this work)'. orchestration.md (all 18 workstreams): '**A wave MUST NOT start** when any of: the previous wave has an unmerged PR; any sibling worktree is un-rebased; the gate is red on `origin/main`; or a `rebase_blocked` marker is unresolved.'

fix.note: Add a Wave 0 task 'get `make ci` green on main' as a hard prerequisite for the whole package, or replace the red-main rule with 'no NEW failures vs. the recorded main baseline' and record that baseline.

findings.problem: Every brief points at a package-level protocol document that does not exist. 212 files in the package reference `docs/agent-tasks/ORCHESTRATION.md` (as `../ORCHESTRATION.md` / `../../ORCHESTRATION.md`), including the line in each brief '(Protocol also in `docs/agent-tasks/ORCHESTRATION.md` — the inline block above is authoritative for this task.)' and the opening line of every workstream orchestration.md 'Read the package-level ../../ORCHESTRATION.md first.' The generated tree contains no such file.
findings.evidence: grep -rc 'ORCHESTRATION.md' <package> | grep -v ':0' | wc -l -> 212. ls of the generated tree: docs/agent-tasks/ contains only todo-completion/; todo-completion/ contains only BREAKDOWN-2026-08-21.md, skeleton.json and the 18 workstream dirs. find for *.md above the workstream dirs -> only BREAKDOWN-2026-08-21.md.

fix.note: Generate docs/agent-tasks/ORCHESTRATION.md (the coordinator protocol is already duplicated verbatim in all 18 workstream files — hoist it), or drop the reference. As shipped, an agent told to 'read the package-level protocol first' hits a missing file on step one.
